segments.title: 1. Photo -> sprite sheet -> in a game
lines: You need: a FRONT photo of your character (one you own / have rights to).
Optional: SIDE and BACK photos (or 3/4) - each becomes its own view.
Pick an output profile for the kind of game (here: kart_racer).
Copy the output folder into the game. Done.
No AI images of people: the studio only cuts out and transforms YOUR photos.

items: Inputs used here. The side + back are SYNTHETIC mannequin renders (labelled) standing in for real photos.

script.cap: Start the studio (run_studio.bat on Windows, or: python sprite_forge_studio.py)
Front photo (use the ... button to browse)
Side photo (optional). Tick 'Side faces left' if it faces left
Back photo (optional). Each view is cut out and aligned to the same height + ground line
Step 2 - output: pick a PROFILE for your kind of game
kart_racer: sprite.png (8 angles), win.png, portrait.png, character.ini - frame size, views and moves are filled in

type: tagline=Built from one photo; speed=4; handling=3.5; weight=medium
script.cap: Profile vars = the game's own ini keys (stats, tagline...). The studio knows nothing about the game itself
Output views = billboard8: missing angles are mirrored or interpolated, and FLAGGED as filled
Building: cutout per view, same height + ground line, 8 angles, sheets, manifests
Done. The preview shows the turnaround: green = real view, orange = filled (mirrored / interpolated)
The log lists every file and every FILLED move or view - nothing is hidden
Your files: out/teal_racer/ (sprite.png, character.ini, views/, turnaround.png ...)

segments.title: Put it in the game
lines: The game picks up any folder with a character.ini (no code changes).
Other engines: pick another profile (Godot, Unity, Tiled, Phaser, platformer...).

segments.title: Limits (honest)
lines: Real photo pixels are used for idle; other moves are labelled placeholders
unless you import frames / a video per move.
Filled angles (45, 135...) are squashed real views - supply 3/4 photos for better ones.
Mirrored views flip text and logos.
Next: video 2 (text -> character + FBX), video 3 (using the sheet / consoles).
